comments.author: whershberger
comments.body:
There are two standing issues with these patches:

- get_global_pool_hard_max_size parses /proc/sys/vm/max_map_count incorrectly, resulting in the default value being used unconditionally
- The default value returned by get_global_pool_hard_max_size is UINT_MAX; a better/conservative choice would be the kernel's default max_map_count (65530)

We've submitted upstream patches to resolve both of these issues; neither have been merged to qemu's master yet.

https://lists.gnu.org/archive/html/qemu-devel/2026-10/msg04337.html

blockers.summary: The sponsor/SRU team asked about the DEP3 header in the jammy patch. The Author field names the uploader, but the Origin commit it cites has a different author, so the attribution is inconsistent. The author has not responded yet.

The Noble debdiff was made on top of 19.2.3, but 19.2.6 is already in -proposed. It needs to be rebased onto the version that is actually current in noble-proposed, or it may conflict or be superseded. The author said they would redo it but has not yet.

The Noble fix cites an upstream PR that is only targeted for 19.2.7, which is not released. The SRU therefore carries an unreleased upstream backport. The Noble patch also has the same DEP3 header issues (unneeded Forwarded field, unclear Author).

The Jammy fix is a custom patch that mixes several upstream sources and is not a straight cherry-pick. The 'Where problems could occur' section relies on the author's own check of call sites for deadlocks, with no independent verification. The reproducer is probabilistic, so a 15-minute run without a crash is weak evidence of the fix.

The description says Quincy and Squid are targeted, but the comments only show debdiffs for Jammy (17.2.9) and Noble (19.2.x). It is unclear which series are covered and whether the UCA releases are handled.
